ocs.mcpjam.com/inspector/evals.md -o evals-doc.md && rg -n 'schemaVersion|toolCall|toolResult|suite file|dialect|assertion|target:
' evals-doc.md | head -60 && rg 'cli/.*[Ee]val|suite.*file|[Aa]ssertion' docs-index.txt\"", "aggregated_output": "7:> Author test
cases for your MCP server, run them across models, and gate pass/fail on deterministic assertions plus optional LLM-as-judge.\n23:
A group of cases plus the defaults they share: attached servers, models to run against, default assertions, judge config, and argu
ment-matching mode.\n27:One scenario you want to verify — a prompt (or a sequence of prompts), the tools you expect to fire, an op
tional expected output, and the assertions that decide pass/fail.\n43:Every case opens in the spine, however it was authored — in
the app, through the CLI, or from an SDK suite file. The spine is a flat, ordered list of steps. Each step is one of:\n45:* **Prom
pt** — a user turn the model receives. The first prompt is always present; use **Add assertion or action** to add a second prompt
for multi-turn cases.\n47:* **Assert** — an assertion that grades the case.\n53:Use **Add assertion or action** to add an assertio
n, a second prompt, or an interact step. Each assertion row says what it checks, who wrote it, and what a miss does:\n56:* **Step
N** — an assertion written as a step (what the CLI and the SDK produce). It is graded in place, at its position in the run, and is
labelled by that position: a step-level \"no tool errors\" reads **No tool errors so far**, because it only sees the transcript u
p to that point. Editing one rewrites that step; it never becomes a case-level assertion.\n57:* **This case** — an assertion you a
dded here. It is graded once, over the finished transcript.\n60:The list reads as a checklist with progressive disclosure. An off
row shows only its short name. Once on, clicking the name opens an inline editor showing the full criterion, the **Required / Advi
sory** role control, and any editable fields (thresholds, match criteria). Multiple editors can stay open at once. An assertion th
at carries a number (such as a latency budget) shows it under the name at rest.\n62:A row's **role** says what a miss does: **Requ
ired** fails the trial, **Advisory** shows the miss without failing it. The control appears when your deployment supports assertio
n policy; otherwise the role chip shows read-only with a tooltip explaining why it cannot be changed — for example, when the asser
tion is inherited from the suite, or when the backend does not yet support assertion policy.\n64:Because a failing required assert
ion halts the run, an assertion written as a step can leave later assertions unrun. The trial column marks those **Skipped**.\n71:
* **No tool should be called** — a negative case. It passes only if the model called nothing. An assertion that requires a tool ca
ll contradicts this, and the spine says so.\n72:* **Any route** — the case names no route and is graded by its assertions. This is
a normal positive case, and it is what most CLI- and SDK-authored cases are.\n74:A brand-new case that asserts nothing at all mus
t answer this question before it can be saved or run: without an assertion, a goal sentence, or a named tool, it would pass vacuou
sly.\n101:The other tabs are unchanged: **Chat**, **Tool Calls** and **Trace** show the transcript, and **Steps** shows execution
order — now with the same assertion names the rest of the page uses and the reason under a failed step.\n114:> A **negative case**
is one you marked **No tool should be called**. Meta questions (\"what params does `search` take?\"), conversational drift, and a
mbiguous prompts are the usual shape. A case that simply names no tool is *not* negative — it is graded by its assertions.\n118:Cl
ick **History** in the trial header to open a list of past iterations. Selecting one freezes the left form on that trial's snapsho
t — the exact steps, assertions, and settings that were in effect when it ran — so you can compare what you see in the trace again
st what was authored at the time.\n161:Some widget interactions send a `ui/message` back to the host (for example, a cart button t
hat says \"Show my cart\") rather than calling a tool directly. During eval execution, these follow-up messages automatically driv
e a continuation model turn — the same way Playground handles them live. The resulting tool call (e.g. `view-cart`) is attributed
to the same `interact` step's turn, so a **Tool was called** assertion on that turn sees the call.\n163:This means an eval case ca
n faithfully verify a full widget interaction sequence: prompt → widget renders → user clicks → model reacts → tool fires → assert
ion passes.\n210:When an assertion is authored on an individual prompt turn it is evaluated against **that turn's slice** of the t
ranscript — tool calls, assistant message, tool errors, and widget observations for that turn only. `Token budget under N` is case
-only because per-turn token usage is not reliably captured; all other assertions are turn-scopable.\n217:> N` remains a valid a
ssertion and keeps working wherever it is already authored,\n224:### Harness system tools in assertion dropdowns\n226:When a suite
is configured to run under a harness host (such as Claude Code or Codex), the tool-name pickers in the case editor also offer the
harness's native **system tools** — for example `bash`, `read`, `webSearch`, `WebFetch` — alongside your MCP server tools. This l
ets you write assertions like **Tool was never called** for `bash` or **Tool was called with…** for `read` without having to type
the wire name by hand.\n228:System tools appear only in assertion pickers. They are not available in pinned tool-call steps or wid
get-assertion \"View (tool)\" selects, because those require a tool that MCPJam can invoke directly.\n502:either a suite file comm
itted to a repository (`mcpjam cloud eval run --file`), or a\n508:One caller is exempt, and only one: the suite file itself. A wri
te that sends\n638:Click a **test case name** to open its definition — the user prompt, checks, and expected outcome. Click a **re
sult cell** (pass/fail) to open a **case drawer** with per-pairing averages (passed count, P50, P95, tokens, calls) and a flat ite
ration list. Click an iteration row to open its full detail view — scorecard, transcript, tool calls, and trace — without leaving
the run page. A **Back** breadcrumb returns to the iteration list. In the scorecard, each evaluator row shows an **Expected** fiel
d (the configured criterion) and an **Actual** field (what the run recorded). When the findings pipeline has produced a narrative
for the iteration, the **Actual** field shows the AI-generated explanation; if the narrative predates the latest grade it is marke
d stale and the recorded evidence is shown instead. Evaluators are grouped by stage rather than split into default and added-asser
tion sections.\n676:The **Generate** button reads your attached servers' tool catalog and drafts realistic cases — a mix of positi
ve (\"call `search` with a query\") and negative (\"don't call `delete_user` on a meta-question\"). Treat it as a draft: skim, edi
t the prompts to match how your users actually talk, tighten the assertions, then save.\n745:3. Delete the ones that don't match r
eal usage; tighten assertions on the rest.\n- [Evaluate](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/evals.md): Author test cases for your M
CP server, run them across models, and gate pass/fail on deterministic assertions plus optional LLM-as-judge.\n- [CLI Overview](ht
tps://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/overview.md): Local MCP testing and mcpjam cloud: probing, debugging, OAuth, conformance, and hosted eva
ls from your terminal\n- [Local Evals](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/local-evals.md): Run an MCPJam eval suite file on your machine
with mcpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity\n- [CI / CD](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/ci.md): Run MCP health checks,
conformance suites, and evals in GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and other CI environments\n- [runSuiteFile](https://docs.mcpjam.com/s
dk/reference/run-suite-file.md): API reference for running an MCPJam suite file locally from code\n- [Resolve or create a file-own
ed eval suite](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/resolve-or-create-a-file-owned-eval-suite.md): Resolve a file-owned
